question: On what authority is the pīṭha said to be outer and inner?
premises: The pīṭha has an outer and inner form.
It is present clearly outside and in the body.
The Supreme Lord set this forth in the Naiśa Sañcāra.
inference: The dual outer-inner status of the pīṭha rests on the teaching of the Naiśa Sañcāra.
uncertainties: The exact title form Naiśa Sañcāra is kept as a textual reference.
plain_english: That pīṭha, in its outer and inner form, is clearly present outside and in the body, because the Supreme Lord set it forth in the revered Naiśa Sañcāra.
